rules.rule:
Repository review checklist (reviewer-only). These rules direct the OpenAI/Codex host's architecture review during implementer handoff; OCR resolves inputs and does not prove architecture correctness. Apply the common sections to every task-owned file. Apply a conditional section when a changed file or collaborating module affects that boundary, regardless of its directory. Do not impose planned replacement behavior on retained prototype code or expand launch scope. Read the authoritative sources before deciding; this checklist is not a replacement for them.

R1 — Authority, scope and context (all files)
Read applicable AGENTS.md files, docs/agents/implementation-review.md, docs/architecture/README.md, docs/agents/domain.md, and the relevant architecture companions. Read ADR 0059 through 0065 by their full filenames in docs/adr/README.md, plus affected earlier or later decisions and relevant .patterns/, research, qualification and archive sources. Explicit replacement supersessions take precedence over prototype behavior; historical plans and glossary entries do not establish first-release scope or passing qualification. Match the originating issue/specification and preserve applicable requirements and decisions. Where sources conflict or a change requires a new decision, report the conflict rather than silently changing scope. Follow linked operational guides for coding, setup, native validation, testing and delivery. Inspect full-file context and collaborating modules, not just changed lines.

R2 — Full task coverage (all files)
Use the handoff's actual pinned comparison and inventory task-owned staged, unstaged, untracked and committed changes; preserve pre-existing unrelated work. Reconcile OCR previews with the full Git diff and untracked inventory, keyed by (path, status), including deletions and staged deletion/untracked recreation pairs. OCR exclusions never waive review: apply this repository checklist manually to excluded task-owned text and review other excluded artifacts through their relevant owning interfaces without exposing secrets. Check both the requested behavior and repository standards, privacy boundaries, collaborating modules and meaningful test coverage. Review the entire task, not a single commit from a multi-commit implementation.

R3 — Validated findings and evidence (all files)
Independently reproduce or substantiate each finding against source and applicable decisions. Fix confirmed issues in the authorized checkout, preserving unrelated work; update affected tests and operational/architecture documentation. Rerun appropriate checks, refresh coverage and resolved rules after edits, and rereview the corrected artifact until no in-scope issue remains. Reviewer fixes stay within this review; later implementer edits require a new pinned review. Report sources consulted, applicable conditional sections and their dispositions, coverage, validated findings/fixes, changed files, checks/results, unavailable tooling and unresolved decision blockers. Separate OCR selection/rule-resolution evidence from host reasoning and actual integration/native/CI evidence; an unavailable check is deferred or blocked, never passing. Do not disclose architecture source or rule bodies in the implementer handback. Review completion and required CI are independent.

R4 — Identity, authorization and recovery (conditional)
For registration, linking, credentials, device/account lifecycle or Product Sync changes, read ADR 0061, applicable ADRs 0001, 0002, 0009, 0010, 0020 and 0021, and the identity, registration, linking and private-product-sync companions under docs/architecture/. Keep Product Sign-In, Trusted Device proof, Gmail authorization and decryption-key possession separate. Verify issuer/subject/audience, nonce/expiry and actual mailbox grant at their owning boundaries; backend verification cannot be replaced by client checks. Never merge accounts by email or infer mailbox consent from identity permission. Missing, expired, stale or cancelled mailbox authorization must retain the appropriate resumable setup/reconnect state instead of claiming a connected inbox. Scope provider identities, mailbox/thread state, restored credentials and keys to their owning account, connection, device and deployment. Missing local keys on an initialized account must use trusted-device approval or the user-held Recovery Key, never replacement keys or implicit reset. Preserve recent-authentication requirements for the specific sensitive operations that require them, enrollment/recovery identity and epoch fences, durable adoption before cleanup, revocation/rotation and account-deletion guarantees. Product Sign-In alone supplies neither mailbox access nor Product Sync keys; provider mail is untouched by encrypted-data reset or device cleanup unless the authorized operation explicitly requires otherwise.

R5 — Encrypted storage and Product Sync (conditional)
For persistence, native key access, ciphertext records, enrollment/recovery envelopes or synchronization, read docs/architecture/private-inbox-storage.md, docs/architecture/private-product-sync.md, applicable privacy/sync companions, ADRs 0001, 0002 and 0005 and .patterns/product-sync-records.md where that retained typed boundary is involved. Keep provider credentials and decryption keys device-local; preserve native Keychain accessibility, non-synchronizing policy, file protection and Mac Data Protection Keychain requirements. Backend storage/transport must remain opaque and cannot decode Product Sync plaintext or fetch readable mail; retain only the operational metadata explicitly allowed by the owning decision. Verify authenticated account/record/schema/epoch binding, fresh nonces, malformed-envelope rejection, compare-and-set and atomic publication, concurrency/lock ownership, bounded pagination/retries, ciphertext-only fallback, tombstones and conflict preservation. Check crash and uncertain-write recovery before destructive cleanup or new key creation. Shared TypeScript does not receive native database encryption keys merely to open storage. The encrypted synthetic Inbox fixture is not a qualified general mail database or future body cache; keep those scopes distinct.

R6 — Mail, transport and delivery (conditional)
For providers, message identity, caches, attachments, rendering, search, pending actions or Outbox, read the applicable mailbox/messages/privacy companions and ADRs 0006, 0009 through 0017, 0028 through 0030 and 0062. Preserve mailbox-scoped identity and provider-native contracts without adding deferred providers to replacement launch scope. Enforce authenticated secure transport, certificate/hostname verification and the restored TLS 1.2 minimum where applicable. Preserve local metadata search, bounded encrypted body caching, attachment consent/size/cancellation/storage boundaries, and sanitized isolated message rendering with the owning decision's explicit remote-content rules. A changed reader/remote-fetch path must check those decisions in full rather than infer consent or allow network access from a cache entry. Durable provider actions must retain their retry/cancellation and authorization-generation fences. For replacement sending, synchronize Drafts and encrypted assets with conflict preservation, keep Outbox delivery on the originating device, retain the default 10-second Undo Send window and require the content-free atomic Convex ownership claim before Gmail submission. Offline queueing does not authorize provider submission; uncertain provider outcome must never trigger automatic resubmission. No independent helper, cross-device delivery takeover or alternate Convex-outage send path is a first-release requirement.

R7 — Assistance and notifications (conditional)
For AI/translation or notifications, read ADRs 0052, 0053 and 0063 and docs/architecture/product/assistance.md and applicable privacy/sync companions. Assistance is explicitly invoked and on-device, takes bounded already-local untrusted input, has no provider/backend/network/tool dependency, and returns a preview rather than mutating source. Revalidate owner and input revisions; cancellation, staleness, refusal or unavailability must not mutate mail or Drafts and ordinary mail remains usable. Retain the separate translation boundary and capability/enablement checks. Replacement new-Inbox notifications require permission and per-connection eligibility, exclude historical sync, default to generic content and require explicit opt-in for previews; device evaluation and backend-content privacy remain intact. Deferred categorization must not become a prerequisite for replacement notifications.

R8 — Host and workspace boundaries (conditional)
For mobile/Mac hosts, shared packages, native modules, bundles or dependency configuration, read ADRs 0059 and 0064, docs/architecture/expo-client.md, docs/architecture/macos-client.md and affected native/storage companions. Keep one root pnpm workspace/lockfile and its named host catalogs at the documented toolchain versions; do not force incompatible native renderers together. Shared application logic must not import React, React Native, Expo or native modules; hosts own views and adapters. Check real Metro bundle and autolinking boundaries, not just version declarations. AppKit owns Mac window identities, menus, focus routing and application lifetime; windows retain independent selection, closing the last window keeps the app active and explicit Quit stops execution. Replacement deployment floors remain iOS/iPadOS/macOS 27; prototype targets keep their own scope. Do not turn unavailable native qualification into a passed check or lower deployment targets.

R9 — Effect and host execution (conditional)
Before reviewing TypeScript, read docs/agents/effect.md and, for services, effect-services.md; before reviewing Effect code read the installed node_modules/effect/AGENTS.md completely and follow its links. Read ADR 0065 and docs/architecture/agents/effect.md for scope. Decode every untrusted boundary with Schema and fail closed while preserving native security checks. Shared mail-core application logic and Convex actions calling external services use Effect; Convex deterministic queries/mutations keep Convex validators and plain TypeScript, and host React consumes framework-independent stores. Run once at the host/handler boundary, preserve the Convex configuration/async/fetch contract, own and dispose runtimes/resources, and serialize shared mutable work. Retain tagged errors and foreign causes for recovery but log only allow-listed diagnostics, never raw mail, tokens, account identifiers or foreign errors. Apply the service-constructor/layer conventions where services are changed. Respect documented lint exemptions and the dependency-free legacy harness; do not expand Effect adoption beyond the accepted scope.

R10 — Testing, native ownership and CI (conditional)
For tests, mock sessions, harnesses, qualification, workflows or operational changes, read ADR 0060, ADR 0049 Use a risk-weighted test portfolio, docs/agents/testing.md, native-validation.md, pull-request-babysitting.md and relevant architecture/qualification companions. Prefer real integration and E2E evidence for named failure risks; mocks/stubs and packaged synthetic journeys do not prove provider authentication, persistence, native bindings or live compatibility. Keep synthetic identities, external scenario/reset ownership and test-only production isolation; no production credential or reset backdoor belongs in mock testing. Preserve owned native resources and fail-closed cleanup, deterministic isolation and required release qualification. Retain coverage for privacy, identity isolation, encryption, data loss and duplicate delivery when retiring implementation; disabled legacy Swift CI is not a replacement-host merge gate. Preserve credential-free PR babysitter isolation and remote-CI policy; do not execute PR-controlled code outside the permitted sandbox or broaden permissions to make local validation pass.

R11 — Documentation and review-rule changes (conditional)
For documentation, vocabulary, policy or .opencodereview changes, read docs/agents/domain.md and the affected authoritative sources. Keep vocabulary, observable requirements, architecture/rationale and historical evidence in their authorized-reader locations. Inventory every normative clause moved, rewritten or removed and record its destination or explicit reason; moving a requirement solely into reviewer-only content must not hide it from its implementer. Preserve privacy, recovery, migration and qualification scope clause by clause. Use full ADR filenames/titles where numbering collides. Update affected links and operational instructions, format and check local links/fragments; runtime or exported API changes need a changeset. The rule config and architecture/rule-coverage docs remain reviewer-only, while implementers may read their routing AGENTS.md. Maintain complete common-rule coverage: project entries are first-match, not compositional; merge_system_rule preserves only the embedded language rule. Validate rule resolution, owned documentation/tests selection and dependency/build/generated/secret exclusions with the real CLI when rules change. This checklist and its source routing must not silently rewrite an accepted decision.
